H1.text: Read out roll number twelve from the class register. You get exactly one name. Never two names, and never no name.

H2.text: Now ask the blood group list: who is group O? You might get two names, or none at all.

H3.text: Aarav noticed this while his teacher took attendance.

H4.text: Why does one list always give a single answer, while the other does not?

H5.text: Because the register is a function: a relation with one strict promise.

D1.text: In NCERT words: a relation f from a set A to a set B is a function if every element of A has one and only one image in B.

D2.text: So there are two checks. First, every element of A must have an image. No element is left without an arrow.

D3.text: Second, each element of A has only one image. No element sends out two arrows.

L1.text: Let us run the function test on three relations from A to B.

L2.text: The first one. One goes to four. Two goes to five. Three also goes to five. Each element sends exactly one arrow. It passes. It is a function.

L3.text: The second one. One sends two arrows, to four and to six. One element, two images. It fails.

L4.text: The third one. Two sends no arrow at all. An element with no image. It fails too.

G1.text: There is a grid picture as well. Put A along the bottom, and B up the side. Each pair is a dot.

G2.text: A function puts exactly one dot in every column. Two dots in one column, or an empty column, and it is not a function.

S1.text: Side by side. Many arrows out of one element of A are not allowed. That element would have two images.

S2.text: But many arrows into one element of B are fine. In the first test, one and two point to different numbers, but two and three share the image five. Still a function.

K1.text: Now you try. Every student is linked to their birth month. Two students share a month. Is it still a function? Pause and think.

K2.text: Yes! Each student still has exactly one birth month. Sharing an image is allowed. Only a student with two months, or none, would break it.

T1.text: Remember this. In a function, every element of A sends exactly one arrow.

V1.text: Functions have their own way of writing.

V2.text: We write f colon A arrow B. It reads: f is a function from A to B.

V3.text: If a comma b is in f, we write f of a equals b. Here b is the image of a under f, and a is the preimage of b.

C1.text: Now, how many functions can we make from A to B? This counting is not in the NCERT text, but JEE asks it.

C2.text: Step one. Say A has p elements, and B has q elements.

C3.text: Step two. Each element of A must pick exactly one image. It has q choices.

C4.text: Step three. The choices are made one after another, and each is free. So the counts multiply.

C5.text: Step four. q times q times q, once for each element of A. That is q to the power p functions.

W2.text: A is one, two, three. B is four, five, six, seven. Is f, with one to four, two to six, three to six, a function? Find f of two.

W3.text: Step one. List the first elements: one, two and three. Every element of A appears.

W4.text: Step two. Each first element appears only once. So each element has one image.

W5.text: Step three. Two and three share the image six. That is allowed.

W6.text: Step four. So f is a function, and f of two equals six.

W7.text: Step five. Five and seven have no preimage. That is allowed too. B does not need to be used up.

X2.text: Many students say f is not a function because five and seven in B get no arrows.

X3.text: But the rule only checks the elements of A. Every element of A has exactly one image, so f is a function.

J1.text: Where is this asked? In PUC exams, as: which of these relations are functions? In JEE Main, as: count the functions that obey a condition.

Q1.text: Exam level now. A is one, two, three. B is one, two, three, four. How many functions f from A to B have f of one not equal to f of two? Pause and solve.

A1.text: The answer is A. Forty eight.

A2.text: With no condition, each of the three elements has four choices. Four cubed is sixty four functions.

A3.text: Now count the ones we do not want, where f of one equals f of two.

A4.text: f of one has four choices, f of two must copy it, and f of three has four choices. That is sixteen.

A5.text: Sixty four minus sixteen leaves forty eight.

F1.text: Here is your recap. Screenshot this card.

Y1.text: Can you answer these three questions without help?

Y2.text: One. Is the relation one comma two, one comma three, two comma four a function from one, two to two, three, four?

Y3.text: Two. How many functions are there from a set of two elements to a set of three elements?

Y4.text: Three. If f of three equals seven, which number is the image, and which is the preimage?
